userStories.title: Close decision gates B1–B4, refresh plan, preflight
userStories.description: As the implementing agent, I want the plan's four blocking decisions recorded in their canonical artifacts and the branch target confirmed, so that all later production work proceeds against one non-conflicting contract.
acceptanceCriteria: B1 is recorded in the owning canonical artifact (ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md AD-7 / EXPERIENCE.md): compatibility-only node-scoped grouping is the default unless a complete first-class aggregate contract is authored covering entry, selection identity, retry/nested-loop/route-activation boundaries, Ask ownership, authorization/visibility boundary, paging, default selection, and a performance budget; the rejected loopParent/'All iterations' design is not used

If B1 lands compatibility-only, the plan and canonical text state explicitly that current loop occurrence rows still show no headings/navigator and Story 2.10 remains blocked on a later reachability decision; if aggregate is accepted, every selection mapper and scope-key consumer (including WorkflowExecution.tsx and RunDetailPage.tsx) is scouted and listed in the plan inventory before editing

B2 is recorded as an adopted design artifact (DESIGN.md / EXPERIENCE.md or clearly adopted doc) covering: control type and relationship to the existing Execution filter; exact copy, placement, sizes, all visible states; pointer/keyboard activation and focus destination; live-poll/scroll-follow and vanished-target behavior; 460px and host small-viewport layout; accessible name, heading relationship, and announcement behavior — no inferred native-select key heuristics

B4 disambiguation rule for colliding derived labels is recorded in the occurrence-grouping authority with concrete examples: two route activations sharing retry_epoch with different route_activation_seq, nested loops whose final ancestry entry repeats, collision plus retry/failed suffixes, and navigator accessible names — never raw UUIDs

B3 branch/PR target is determined from git evidence (origin HEAD and open PRs use develop; local dev is ~68 commits behind and untracked) and the stale repository authority is corrected so plan, CI, and PR base agree; the decision is recorded

plan.md is updated with the recorded decisions: verified behavior table, file inventory, acceptance criteria, test list, performance budget, compatibility, and rollback sections all reflect the outcome

Preflight is recorded: issue #180 and sprint state checked, git status/branch/base/active worktrees/open PRs surveyed (PR #202 overlap noted), focused green baselines re-run, and confirmation that no production file carries unrelated user changes
No production source file is modified in this story

userStories.title: Occurrence-safe projection and pure grouping core
userStories.description: As a Web transcript renderer, I want execution identity preserved on every history item, text projection that cannot merge across occurrences, and a pure occurrence-grouping module, so that shells can group deterministically without touching the wire.
acceptanceCriteria: TranscriptExecution is derived from NodeMessageRow['metadata']['execution'] (no hand-copied wire interface) and a required `execution: TranscriptExecution | null` field exists on every AgentHistoryItem variant (assistant, tool, lifecycle); historical rows produce execution: null on every variant

agent-history.test.ts covers: assistant items carry projected message execution; lifecycle items carry message execution; paired tools carry call execution; standalone result carries result execution; old rows yield null; existing todo folding, interrupted folding, outcome, and presentation expectations unchanged except the added field

project-text-transcript.ts includes occurrence and attempt ids in keyed stream correlation identity and resets anonymous delta accumulation when execution identity changes; tests prove identical stream_id/message_id/block_id across different occurrences or attempts never merge while same-identity merges behave as today; a metadata-less historical sequence preserves current behavior; inputs are not mutated; no UUID regexes are added (server/DB schemas already validate)

packages/web/src/lib/occurrence-groups.ts is new and pure: one pass over items in transcript sequence order, Map<occurrence_id, accumulator> + ordered group array, leading unkeyed items in prefixItems, unkeyed items after the first key join the nearest preceding group, a repeated non-contiguous key rejoins its original group, fresh arrays/objects returned, showHeaders = groups.length >= 2; no React, DOM, shell tokens, provider branches, parsing, or network

Label composer: final loop-ancestry entry -> `Iteration N` (no suffix); otherwise retry_epoch (absent treated as 0) + 1 -> `Run N`, `· retry` when epoch > 0, `· failed` only when that occurrence contains a failed lifecycle state; B4 rule disambiguates colliding base labels; attempt_id, raw UUIDs, agent-authored text, and provider names never appear in labels

occurrence-groups.test.ts covers all 13 planned cases: no keyed items -> all prefix/no groups; one occurrence -> showHeaders=false; two occurrences -> unique groups ordered by first appearance; epochs 0/1 -> `Run 1`, `Run 2 · retry`; failed retry suffix composition per adopted UX text; final ancestry entry -> `Iteration N`; B4 route/nested collisions -> distinct labels; same occurrence different attempts -> one group; unkeyed item after a group joins it; unkeyed items before first key stay in prefixItems; non-contiguous key rejoins first group with every item exactly once and per-group order preserved; model text `Run 99`/`Iteration 99` never affects labels; inputs not mutated
Pass: (cd packages/web && bun test src/lib/project-text-transcript.test.ts src/lib/agent-history.test.ts src/lib/occurrence-groups.test.ts)
Pass: (cd packages/web && bun run type-check)
No fetch, selection-helper, renderer, scroll, or product-copy change lands in this story

userStories.title: Occurrence headings on all three history consumers
userStories.description: As an operator, I want each displayed occurrence rendered under its own semantic heading on the Legacy Node Room, Console Node Room, and Console inline execution history, so that multi-occurrence transcripts are readable without changing row anatomy.
acceptanceCriteria: Post-PR-#202 versions of NodeRoom.tsx, NodeTranscriptPane.tsx, ConsoleAgentHistoryList.tsx, ConsoleNodeRoom.tsx, ConsoleExecutionHistory.tsx and their tests are re-read before editing; if merged shapes differ from the plan inventory, the plan inventory is updated first and unrelated behavior is preserved

NodeTranscriptPane computes the grouping from items; NodeRoom keeps its current flat path when showHeaders=false; for multiple groups it renders prefixItems first with no heading, then one semantic heading at the B2-approved level per group followed by the group's existing item rendering; renderAfterItem, partial-load notice, retry, and renderAtEnd keep their current logical positions

Console: one small pure renderability predicate (visible under showToolCalls/showSystem) is extracted and shared by the list, room, and inline execution history; a group is displayable iff it has a visible item OR a hidden tool item with an attached Ask card that still renders; headings (and later navigator options) derive from the same displayable group list; fewer than two displayable groups -> existing flat/error/empty behavior
ConsoleExecutionHistory renders headings only — never the node-room navigator; unanchored Ask/approval extras remain after history and create no synthetic occurrence group

Heading styling matches DESIGN.md exactly on both shells: 10.5px mono uppercase, 0.08em tracking, text-secondary, 10px 0 5px margin, flex label plus 1px border rule to the right edge; label remains plain text in the accessibility tree; stable React keys and any DOM id use occurrence_id (useId-namespaced), never array index

Paired tests in NodeRoom.test.tsx and ConsoleNodeRoom.test.tsx use the same test names/assertion intent: zero/one occurrence -> no headings and no navigator; two occurrences -> two headings at approved level in group order with exact core labels; colliding base labels -> distinct B4-approved names; multiple attempts in one occurrence -> no extra heading; leading unscoped prefix renders once before the first heading; non-contiguous rows render once under one unique heading; per-group assistant/tool/lifecycle order stable; renderAfterItem/renderAtEnd placement preserved; partial-page error/retry and unknown-scope warning still visible; label text from item content cannot alter headings

Console-specific tests: hiding system/tool rows removes a group only when no row or attached Ask remains renderable; an Ask attached to a hidden tool keeps group + Ask visible without the tool row; dropping to one displayable group removes all headings and navigator options; ConsoleExecutionHistory follows the same visibility rule and never renders the navigator

LegacyNodeRoom.test.tsx still compiles for its direct NodeRoom mount pattern (updated only for actual post-merge public props); console-isolation.test.ts stays green; no Console module imports from @/components/; no new design tokens or one-use component files

Pass: (cd packages/web && NODE_ENV=development bun test src/components/workflows/NodeRoom.test.tsx src/components/workflows/NodeTranscriptPane.test.tsx src/components/workflows/LegacyNodeRoom.test.tsx) and (cd packages/web && NODE_ENV=development bun test src/experiments/console/components/ConsoleNodeRoom.test.tsx src/experiments/console/components/inspect/ConsoleExecutionHistory.test.tsx src/experiments/console/console-isolation.test.ts)
Pass: (cd packages/web && bun run type-check) and bun run lint --max-warnings 0

userStories.title: B2-approved occurrence navigator on both node rooms
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the approved occurrence navigator on the Legacy and Console node rooms, so that I can jump directly to an occurrence section while follow, scroll, and focus behavior stay well-defined.
acceptanceCriteria: Navigator mounts at the B2-approved location with approved copy/control type on both NodeTranscriptPane (Legacy) and ConsoleNodeRoom (Console); options derive only from the rendered occurrence headings and target headings by stable occurrence_id

Interaction with live follow and restored scroll is modeled as an explicit reducer/state transition — not an ignoreNextScroll-style event-suppression heuristic; room-scroll-follow.ts is changed only if the B2-approved behavior requires a new explicit transition
The navigator stays independent of 'Jump to latest' and the existing Execution filter; Execution filtering and request scope are unchanged (unless B1 authorized a tested aggregate model)
When scope/filter/poll removes the current target, state is reset or reconciled exactly as B2 specifies — no stale value or dead target
Pointer, keyboard, focus-visible, and screen-reader announcement behavior match the B2 contract on both shells; no browser-specific native-select key heuristics are encoded

All eight scroll/follow cases from the plan are covered by reducer and shell tests: navigation while a live transcript is pinned; a new row arriving after navigation; reader-initiated scroll after navigation; 'Jump to latest' restoring follow; saved scrollTop across room close/reopen; already-visible/clamped target; target removed by scope or Console filters; focus behavior on pointer and every supported keyboard path
Paired Legacy/Console tests produce identical outcomes; navigator is absent at zero or one displayable group

If B2 changed the existing Execution control instead of adding a second control, NodeRoomHeader.tsx / ConsoleRoomHeader.tsx, their options model, E2E contracts, and the file inventory were re-scouted and updated before editing

Pass: (cd packages/web && NODE_ENV=development bun test src/components/workflows/NodeRoom.test.tsx src/components/workflows/NodeTranscriptPane.test.tsx src/components/workflows/LegacyNodeRoom.test.tsx) and the Console suite from phase-02 validation
Pass: (cd packages/web && bun run type-check) and bun run lint --max-warnings 0

userStories.title: Integration evidence, visual/a11y matrix, doc sync, and PR handoff
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want end-to-end evidence matching the B1 reachability mode, synchronized canonical docs, an honest acceptance report, and all repository gates green, so that Story 1.7 can ship via the normal PR workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: Integration evidence matches the recorded B1 mode — compatibility-only: occurrence/attempt network assertions stay green (selecting an occurrence sends exact filters and yields one group, no headings/navigator), component tests are the primary multi-occurrence proof, and any Playwright seeded/intercepted fixture is labelled renderer-integration evidence, not server reachability; aggregate: a real path selects the aggregate view through its approved UI entry with an unambiguous request/selection identity, retry/nested-loop/route/Ask isolation proven, no cross-run/cross-node or authorization broadening, identifiers-only error logging, and page-count/render-timing recorded against the 3,465-row seven-occurrence sample vs. the approved budget

Regression evidence preserved: selecting two individual iterations still issues two distinct occurrence-filtered requests; Execution select filters/refetches and persists selection; pagination high-watermark/refresh/scope-abort/partial-failure behavior unchanged; todos pinned; Ask cards scoped/anchored/actionable; live follow, manual hold, restored scroll, 'Jump to latest'; Console tool/system toggles and Console import isolation all green

Visual matrix captured on both shells for all nine planned states (unscoped flat, single occurrence flat, multiple retry occurrences with correct suffixes, multiple loop occurrences `Iteration N`, colliding route/nested labels resolved, Console filtered to one displayable group, partial/error with loaded groups, live append after navigation, target removed on filter/scope change) at: 460px authoritative room width (10.5px mono uppercase, 0.08em, text-secondary, 10px 0 5px, 1px rule, no horizontal overflow, unchanged row wrapping) and the host small-viewport breakpoint (actual viewport recorded; transcript adds no breakpoint, control stays operable), plus B2-defined focus-visible states on both shells

Accessibility evidence is automated: one heading at the B2-approved level per rendered occurrence with exact visible name, no heading on prefix/unkeyed content; navigator accessible name/state/relationship per B2; DOM/accessibility order matches visual order; keyboard-only traversal and activation identical on both shells; navigation causes no per-row live-region announcements; unavailable manual AT environments recorded as unavailable, not passed

Documentation synced to the accepted decisions only: EXPERIENCE.md distinguishes the filtering Execution control from the Story 1.7 navigator (navigation/focus behavior per B2); AD-7 and the IA section amended only if B1 adopted the aggregate contract (never the rejected loopParent workaround); DESIGN.md and adopted mocks agree with superseded wording removed; no generated types, schemas, unrelated specs, or sprint-status files edited; every doc link and claimed path verified against code/tests

reports/acceptance.md maps every acceptance criterion to its evidence: test name + command, evidence type (pure/component/renderer-integration/real E2E), screenshot/AX artifact where applicable, actual viewport/room width, B1 reachability mode and explicit limitation, aggregate perf numbers if applicable

All gates pass: the three focused bun test commands from the plan, (cd packages/web && bun run type-check), bun run lint --max-warnings 0, (cd e2e && bun run typecheck), the B1-specific Playwright command(s) recorded at the gate, and bun run validate — never root bun test

PR opened on the B3-confirmed branch using .github/pull_request_template.md explicitly (required sections kept, instructional comments and unused sections deleted), conventional title `feat(web): navigate transcript occurrences` (adjusted if B1 added a reviewed public contract), `Closes #180` included only when all accepted issue criteria are actually met; no sprint-status mutation
